alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive verb takes the connective the ASV wrote for it, *So* (rule 14).
Finite verb takes its lexical verb; the explicit subject noun is its own unit (rule 17).
Proper name.
Waw → *and* (rule 14).
Numeral takes only its own word (rule 15).
Construct noun keeps its own word; the possessive is the suffix's (rule 18).
Suffix → *his* (rule 18), reordered before the numeral under rule 25.
Waw → *and* (rule 14).

Construct chain נֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו rendered by the single English word *armorbearer*, which writes both lexemes; fused under rule 30 and headed on the construct, the governing morpheme, under rule 23's tie ruling. The suffix is outside the fusion and takes *his*.
Suffix → *his* (rule 18).

No waw stands before כָּל־אֲנָשָׁיו; the ASV's *and* is what it wrote for the additive particle גַּם, read off the ASV under rule 14's open connective list rather than marked `added`. Competing reading: גַּם unrepresented and *and* `added` under rule 14's asyndeton sentence; rejected because a present morpheme carrying the additive sense licenses the word (rule 11).
כֹּל → *all*.
Noun keeps its own word.
Suffix → *his* (rule 18).
The ASV writes the temporal phrase bare (*that same day*) with no preposition, so the בְּ is unrepresented under rule 40.
Assimilated article on the noun; the ASV writes *that* for the demonstrative and no *the*, so the article is unrepresented under rule 41 (as in הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא → *that place*).
Noun → *day*.
Agreement article on the demonstrative; unrepresented under rules 41 and 47.

Demonstrative הוּא takes the written *that* (rule 41); *same* is the ASV's emphatic expansion of that one demonstrative's identifying force and is placed with it rather than marked `added`, on the reasoning rule 20 gives for a doubled demonstrative realization. Competing reading: *same* as its own `added` unit under rule 30.
Adverb → *together*.

review_notes: Every source and target ID partitioned once. The one notable choice is *and* for גַּם (no waw in that phrase) and *same* joined to the demonstrative; both competing readings are named in the unit notes.
